transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I've just been feeling so tired all the time, and I've no energy for anything. It's been getting me down, truth be told.
When did you first start feeling this tired?
Since last week, I'd say.
Have you ever had an allergy or a bad reaction to any medicine?
Yes, codeine makes me very sick. I can't take it at all.
On a scale from 0 to 10, where 0 means no tiredness and 10 means the worst tiredness you can imagine, how bad is your tiredness?
I'd put it at about a 3 out of 10. I've had to stop my swimming twice a week, which I'm not happy about.
Are you taking any medicines at the moment, either regularly or just recently?

I take metformin twice a day for my diabetes, and levothyroxine every morning for my thyroid. I've also been on omeprazole for years for indigestion, and I take ibuprofen most days for a sore shoulder.
When did you first start feeling this tired?
Well, thinking about it more, it's actually been coming on gradually over about two months now, not just last week. I must have got that muddled earlier.
Just to be clear, you first said the tiredness started last week, and then you said it’s been coming on gradually over about two months — which of those would you say is more accurate?
The two months is the right one. It's crept up on me slowly, I just wasn't thinking straight the first time you asked.
Have you noticed anything that seems to make your tiredness better or worse?
It's there all day really, but it seems worse in the afternoon. I've started needing a nap most days now, which I never used to do.
Apart from what you've already told me, is there anything else about your past health, like other long-term conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays?
I've had type 2 diabetes for about 12 years, and I've got an underactive thyroid as well. I haven't had any operations or hospital stays that I can think of.
Besides feeling tired and down, is there anything else you'd like to add?
I do get more short of breath than usual going up hills, and a couple of friends have said I look a bit pale. I suppose what worries me most is whether I'll be able to keep looking after my husband.
Would you say the tiredness feels like it sits mostly in one part of your body, like your arms or legs, or is it more of a whole-body feeling, or are you not sure?
I can't say it's in any one place — it's just a general feeling all over, like I've no energy in me at all.
Is there anything that makes your tiredness better or worse, like resting, being more active, or eating, or are you not sure?

Resting doesn't really seem to help much — even after a nap I don't feel refreshed. Being active makes it worse, that's part of why I gave up the swimming. I haven't noticed eating making much difference.
And if you had to describe the tiredness itself — what does it actually feel like to you?
It's hard to describe really — it's just a heavy, flat sort of tiredness, like I've got nothing in the tank. I sleep about seven hours but wake up feeling unrefreshed, as if I've not slept at all.
Is there anything else about your past health that you'd like to add?
No, I don't think there's anything else — just the diabetes and the thyroid, and the indigestion I've had for years.
Are there any other medicines you take, including ones you buy without a prescription, that we haven't talked about yet?
No, that's everything — the metformin, levothyroxine, omeprazole and the ibuprofen I buy from the chemist for my shoulder. I don't take anything else.
Is there anything else you've noticed that seems new or different lately?
I have noticed I'm struggling more with helping my husband wash and dress in the mornings — that's got harder. And my mood feels a bit flat with all the caring, I suppose.
Is there anything else you've noticed along with the tiredness that you haven't mentioned yet?
I don't think so — I've not had any chest pain, I've not lost any weight, and my bowels have been normal. Just the tiredness, the breathlessness on hills and feeling pale.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
